title: Compatibility window and backwards testing matrix for v0 -> Unified transport transition
creator: Anika Bose
description: Goal: Define a bounded compatibility window, an exhaustive backwards-compatibility test matrix, and telemetry gates to safely transition customers from v0-era transport/endpoints to the Unified inference transport (single unified generate/chat/embed API). This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout milestones, and the testing matrix that engineering and QA must implement before the deprecation notice is broadly published.
background: We are consolidating multiple historical transports (SSE chunked streaming, legacy longpoll, legacy synchronous batch endpoints and v0-style model aliases) into a single Unified transport and routing model. Prior deprecation work focused on rollout playbooks; this ticket focuses on defining the compatibility window, the exact set of client behaviors we must support during the transition, and the automated tests/telemetry that will gate rollouts to customers.
scope: Define a compatibility window (start/end dates) and customer notice schedule
Create a backwards-compatibility test matrix covering: SSE chunked streaming, short-lived websockets, longpoll fallbacks, synchronous batch embeddings, and v0 model alias resolution
Define automated integration tests that run in CI and in pre-production canaries
Specify telemetry events, thresholds, and rollback gates
Produce a migration guidance doc and client checklists for SDK teams and partner integrators
out_of_scope: Implementation of SDK-side automated migration helpers (separate SDK workstreams will own this),
Billing or pricing changes associated with the migration
Major behavioral changes to model outputs beyond transport/protocol compatibility
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility window and customer notice calendar published in Confluence
Comprehensive test matrix created and approved by QE and runtime eng leads
CI jobs exist that exercise all matrix permutations (transport x client-version x model-alias) and pass in preprod
Telemetry shows <0.5% increase in 5xx or timeout errors for canary customers during a 14-day pilot
Customer-facing migration guide with deterministic client checklists, sample curl/SDK snippets, and rollback instructions published
Runbook for on-call with clear escalation paths and automated rollback triggers documented
migration_timeline: 2026-03-15: Publish compatibility window proposal to stakeholders and legal for review
2026-03-31: Approve test matrix and CI integration plan
2026-04-15: Implement preprod CI matrix and initial telemetry dashboards (canary metrics)
2026-05-01: Start 2-week canary with 5 internal customers and two pilot partners
2026-05-20: Evaluate canary against gating thresholds; if green, open public opt-in migration for non-critical customers
2026-06-01: Start staged enforcement (soft-fail warnings then hard enforcement) for older transports per rollout strategy
2026-06-30: End of compatibility window — final enforcement unless rollback/extension approved
telemetry_and_gates: Heartbeat / connection success rate per transport (SSE, websocket, longpoll, sync-batch)
Per-transport 5xx and 4xx rates (goal: no >0.5% regression vs baseline)
Per-customer error spike detector (alert if > 3x baseline for 1 hour)
Latency distribution changes 50/95/99 percentiles (no regression >10% p95)
Migration adoption metric: percent of active API keys upgraded to Unified transport by week
Gate behavior: If any gate breaches during Canary, pause rollout and execute rollback plan
rollout_strategy: Phase 0 (internal): runs against synthetic workloads and internal customers
Phase 1 (pilot): invite opt-in customers and select partners; monitor telemetry closely
Phase 2 (soft enforcement): issue warning headers and admin console notices to impacted customers but keep backward compatibility enabled
Phase 3 (hard enforcement): enforce transport mapping with 30-day grace for exceptions; customers can request extensions via support
Phase 4 (sunset): fully disable legacy transport endpoints after the compatibility window closes
rollback_plan: If telemetry gates fail during any rollout phase we will immediately revert the routing policy for affected customers to the previous v0 mapping, reopen capacity in the legacy routing tier, and roll back any schema-level enforcement. The rollback runbook will include step-by-step commands, affected service list, communication templates for customers, and post-mortem requirements.
dependencies: ENG-35678 (telemetry: new canary dashboards and alerting rules)
ENG-36102 (CI: matrix orchestration and environment provisioning)
notes: Prior deprecation playbooks focused on high-level timelines; this ticket must produce machine-readable tests and telemetry gates that engineering can rely on. We should avoid a single global cutoff date without per-customer exceptions and clearly documented support SLAs. Coordinate with legal for notice language and with SDK teams for sample migrations.
